title: ai says /ay/
parentNote: Today is the same sound as yesterday, spelled a different way. ay and ai both say the name of the letter a, and English simply keeps two spellings for it — rain and day, tail and play. That is not a muddle to fix; it is the first time your child meets the fact that one sound can have more than one spelling, and the rest of this stage is built on it. There is a rule, and it is worth saying out loud: ai goes in the middle of a word, ay goes on the end. So rain, not rayn; day, not dai. The slip to expect is the a and the i being sounded apart, so rain comes out ra-in, in two pieces. Cover the i, say the a alone, then uncover and say the whole word once, as one sound. Reading it is today's job — spelling it correctly will take months, and that is normal.

activities.mouthCue: Exactly the same mouth as yesterday: open wide, then slide shut.
activities.prompt: Listen hard. This team says the same thing as yesterday's team, ay. Two letters, one sound, the name of the letter a: ai.

Three sounds. The team sits in the middle, with a sound on each side of it.
The longest one. Four sounds, and two of them crowd together on the end.

activities.title: Rain on the paint
activities.prompt: Read the story one line at a time. Tap any word you want to hear again.
lines: I did want to paint a train, and Fern did get the red tin.
Fern and I sat in the garden with a big sheet.
I did paint the train and its long black track.
Big drips fell on the sheet, and the red paint ran.
I did wail. The train is a mess!
But Fern did grin, and did dip her brush in the wet red trail.
Drip, drip, drip. Fern and the rain did paint the sheet red.
It is not a train. It is a big red storm.
Fern did stick it up in the barn. It is the best thing I did paint.
